_doc: Tests the PR suite job tolerates. skips: a test that SKIPS itself (name as the TAP prints it). knownFail: a test that is red on the hosted runner for a runner reason; tolerated only when EVERY failed test is listed. Both need a reason; anything else fails the job. Measured 2026-11-24: 3 skips (btrfs) + 5 knownFail (4 uid-1000 + 1 ext4 inode-reuse flake) of 9251 tests.

skips.name: \#149 the watch survives a WAL inode recycle (unlink + recreate at a new inode)
skips.reason: src/main/bus-wake-watcher.test.ts skips itself loudly: the recycle arm needs $HOME on btrfs to be non-vacuous; the runner's $HOME is ext4 (measured 2026-11-24, 3 skips of 9250 tests).

skips.name: \#93: appendInboxBlock reads exactly N blocks under concurrent large appends
skips.reason: src/shared/inbox-blocks.test.ts skips itself loudly: 'scratch fs is ext4, not btrfs — the splice needs a real fs'; the runner checkout is ext4.

skips.name: \#93 CONTROL (the pre-fix mutant): a bare appendFile OVER-COUNTS — proving the rig discriminates
skips.reason: same btrfs requirement as the #93 test above (its must-FAIL control arm).

knownFail.name: relay killed mid-session (SIGUSR2): the keeper restarts it and the next create is labelled
knownFail.reason: src/keeper/keeper-docker-relay.test.ts:352 asserts the restarted relay's socket INODE differs ('the socket must be a NEW listener'); ext4 reuses a freed inode number, so it fails ~1 run in 3 on the runner (the docker-relay rig's kill_relay arm fails on the same check); the btrfs dev machine never reuses. Flaky on the runner only (measured 2026-11-24).
